The two groundings do not compete: the note's own second sentence would grant this break even in a hypothetical future model where each base character carried its own distinct, declared group, since `same_run_refusal` permits two occurrences declared in different groups exactly as the note's own second sentence already requires regardless of group (`same_run_refusal`'s own doc) — so this case does not rest on the adjudicated reading being the only route to the right answer, only on the reading and the note's own broader permission agreeing, which they do.

The two inputs differ in exactly one declared field — `style`, `"mono"` there against `"jukugo"` here — and an implementation that refuses every same-run boundary a `ruby` construct declares, without reading which style it declared, passes the mono case and fails this one: §C.2#7 denies a break anywhere inside a simple-ruby complex without exception, while §C.2#8's own second sentence grants one between two base characters of the *same* jukugo-ruby complex explicitly. Collapsing the two notes into one same-run rule is the asymmetry this pair of cases exists to catch.

cases.quote: A line break opportunity exists between two consecutive base characters belonging to different jukugo-ruby character complexes (cl-23).
cases.rationale: The note's own first sentence: two jukugo-ruby complexes set side by side, reusing `A.23/two-complexes/second-complex-first-base`'s own input — 東西南北 with two annotation streams (`とうざい`, `なんぼく`) and two `constructs.ruby` entries, each declaring `style: "jukugo"` over one complex — with `kind` changed and one candidate declared at the seam between them. `overlay_of` allocates a fresh `RunId` per declared array entry, so the two complexes convert to two distinct runs despite sitting immediately adjacent with nothing between them, the identical mechanism `C.2/two-ornamented-complexes-adjacent/break-permitted` and `C.2/two-simple-ruby-complexes-adjacent/break-permitted` exercise for `ornaments` and simple-ruby above. The candidate sits at that adjacency, at the identical blank cl-19 coordinate every one of this round's own six cases measures, and the note's own first sentence grants the break there — the complement to `C.2/two-base-characters-in-one-jukugo-ruby-complex/break-permitted`'s own second sentence, the two together covering both of §C.2#8's own permissive halves. Only the note's third sentence, ruby-to-ruby indivisibility, is outside what a base-only item stream can measure — `same_run_refusal`'s own doc and `overlay_of`'s own doc above both state why, and no case in this file claims otherwise.

forbidden.why: Treating every base character carrying `style: "jukugo"` ruby as one run regardless of which `constructs.ruby` array entry declared it — the identical failure the two adjacent-complex cases above name for `ornaments` and simple-ruby, reached here through jukugo-ruby instead. §C.2#8's own first sentence grants the break between two *different* jukugo-ruby complexes; refusing it here collapses the two declared array entries into one complex the case never asked for.
